title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Hydrostatic pressure can raise Eu(III) quantum yield by shortening the ligand–metal distance, strengthening hydrogen bonds and π–π contacts, suppressing nonradiative decay, and improving energy transfer.
explanation: For Eu(BTC) hydrate, the review reports that these structural compressions act together and gives a photoluminescence quantum yield of 69.1% at 9.2 GPa.
scope: Compressible europium carboxylate MOFs, specifically Eu(BTC) hydrate.
conditions: High pressure, with the stated performance at 9.2 GPa.
caveats: The numerical PLQY is for this framework under pressure; ambient reversibility and generality to other Eu-MOFs are not established in the review.
